question: A pipe can fill a cistern in 20 minutes, but an outlet can empty it in 28 minutes. When both the pipes are opened, in what time is the cistern filled?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Capacity** of the cistern = LCM of 20 and 28 = 140 units.

Efficiency of **Filling Pipe** = 140 ÷ 20 = +7 units/min.

Efficiency of **Emptying Pipe** = 140 ÷ 28 = −5 units/min.

Net Efficiency when both open = 7 − 5 = 2 units/min.

Time required = Total Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency = 140 ÷ 2 = 70 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time to fill (x) = 20 min

Time to empty (y) = 28 min

**Formula Used:**

Net Work done in 1 minute = (1/x − 1/y)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae04e14860cbd44c2ce77bd76bfcf195f68057f8a79848fbef80644fbd7c8cf4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done by filling pipe in 1 min = 1/20

⇒ Work done by emptying pipe in 1 min = 1/28

⇒ Net work done in 1 min = 1/20 − 1/28

⇒ Net work = (7 − 5) / 140

⇒ Net work = 2 / 140 = 1 / 70

⇒ Total time taken to fill the cistern = 70 min

The calculated value matches **Option (4)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Rate Formula

If pipe A fills a tank in x hours and pipe B empties it in y hours (where y > x), then the net time taken to fill the tank is (x × y) ÷ (y − x).

Work Sign Convention

In **Pipes and Cisterns**, work done by an inlet pipe is taken as positive (+), and work done by an outlet pipe (leakage) is taken as negative (−).

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken by two pipes is a:b, then the ratio of their efficiency is b:a.</p
